findings.title: Denial-cache keys are ambiguous for valid resource and folder UIDs
findings.body: The key concatenates `action`, `name`, and `parent` using `_` without escaping or length-prefixing the variable fields. Dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so a denial for `(name="a_b", parent="c")` produces the same key as `(name="a", parent="b_c")` for the same user/action/namespace. Once the first request is denied, the second request is returned as denied directly from the cache for 30 seconds even if its database permissions allow it. Use an unambiguous encoding of the individual fields (and preferably a distinct denial-cache key prefix).

findings.title: Per-resource denial entries allow unbounded cache growth from request input
findings.body: Every denied `Check` inserts a distinct cache entry keyed by the caller-supplied resource name and parent folder. Unlike the permission cache, whose cardinality is bounded roughly by users and actions, this cache can be populated with arbitrary nonexistent names by repeatedly issuing authorization checks. The configured TTL only bounds retention to 30 seconds and the local cache configuration has no capacity limit here, so sufficient request volume can create a large transient memory footprint (and equivalent key churn in a shared cache). Bound this cache by size/admission policy, avoid caching arbitrary nonexistent resource names, or otherwise rate-limit/normalize these entries.
